recaps.title: Session 1 Recap: Welcome to the Magical World of Godot! 🏰

sections.heading: 🧱 What are Nodes and Scenes?
sections.text: A Node is the primary building block in Godot, like a small colorful Lego piece! We combine these blocks to create a Scene, representing a complete room or level in our game!

sections.heading: 🏗️ Parent-Child Hierarchy
sections.text: Children follow parents! A Child node inherits all properties and coordinates from its Parent node, moving together inside the Godot world smoothly!

recaps.title: Session 2 Recap: Secret Codes and Smart Variables! 📝

sections.heading: 📦 Smart Variables Box
sections.text: We use the var keyword to create smart boxes storing values like int whole numbers, float decimals, or bool logic choices!

sections.heading: ⏳ ready and process Functions
sections.text: The ready() function runs once at the beginning to wake up nodes, while the process() function runs repeatedly to update movement at lightning speed!

recaps.title: Session 3 Recap: The Little Artist and Animated Sprites! 🎨

sections.heading: 🖌️ Game Art & Styles
sections.text: We learned about retro Pixel Art, cartoonish styles, and hand-drawn visuals that make our game world beautiful and friendly!

sections.heading: 🏃‍♀️ Frame-by-Frame Animations
sections.text: We used AnimatedSprite nodes to chain consecutive animation frames from a single Sprite Sheet, making our character walk and jump smoothly!

recaps.title: Session 4 Recap: Speedy Bunny and Smart Operators! 🐰

sections.heading: ➕ Arithmetic & Operators
sections.text: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division are mathematical tools we use in GDScript to calculate speed, double scores, or reverse directions!

sections.heading: 📐 Sizing and set_scale
sections.text: We studied logical comparisons like and/or to control when actions happen, and utilized the set_scale function to shrink or grow nodes!

recaps.title: Session 5 Recap: Journey of a Game from Idea to Light! 💡🌱

sections.heading: 🗺️ The 6 Steps of SDLC
sections.text: A game developer brainstorms Ideas, creates a simple Prototype, designs visual assets, codes the game, tests for bugs, and finally releases it!

sections.heading: 🔬 Prototyping & Playtesting
sections.text: Prototyping ensures our gameplay is fun, while thorough testing resolves unexpected crashes and bugs to please our players!

recaps.title: Session 6 Recap: Magical Buttons and Colorful Panels! 🖥️

sections.heading: 📝 Labels and Buttons
sections.text: Labels display dynamic game texts (scores, health, warnings), while Buttons let players interact with the game with a single click!

sections.heading: 📦 Organizing layouts with Containers
sections.text: Layout containers like VBoxContainer and HBoxContainer automatically organize UI items vertically or horizontally in a clean grid!

recaps.title: Session 7 Recap: Signal Language and Interactive Buttons! 📡

sections.heading: 📡 Signals System
sections.text: Signals are like internal phones in Godot, enabling a node like a Button to send a pressed() signal to execute corresponding codes!

sections.heading: 🔄 Scene Transitions & Exit
sections.text: We switch scenes smoothly in GDScript using get_tree().change_scene(), and exit the application instantly using get_tree().quit()!

recaps.title: Session 8 Recap: Joyful Sounds and Dreamy Music! 🎵

sections.heading: 💥 SFX vs Background Music
sections.text: Sound effects (SFX) play short triggers upon jumping or bouncing, while background music (BGM) loops to create a magical atmosphere!

sections.heading: 🎛️ Audio Nodes & Controls
sections.text: We use AudioStreamPlayer2D nodes to hold sound files, adjusting volume and pitch, and running play() and stop() methods!

recaps.title: Session 9 Recap: Magic Camera and Moving Backgrounds! 📸🌌

sections.heading: 📸 Camera2D and Smoothing
sections.text: The Camera2D follows the player smoothly when smoothing is turned on, keeping the camera centered on the active world player!

sections.heading: 🌌 Parallax Background & preload()
sections.text: ParallaxBackground layer scales move far backgrounds slower to create depth, and preload() loads scenes in advance to avoid lag!

recaps.title: Session 10 Recap: Polishing Games and Launching to the Universe! 🚀✨

sections.heading: ✨ Game Polishing
sections.text: Polishing makes games feel complete by boosting responsiveness, increasing fun factor, and removing minor visual glitches!

sections.heading: 🌐 Web Exporting & itch.io
sections.text: Exporting games to HTML5 format prepares web-ready files, allowing us to upload and share our games freely on itch.io!

recaps.title: Session 11 Recap: Birth of the Legendary Pong Game - Part 1! 🏓

sections.heading: 🧱 Collisions & Kinematic Bodies
sections.text: We designed solid outer boundaries using StaticBody2D nodes, and built moving paddles and ball using KinematicBody2D nodes!

sections.heading: ⌨️ Player Input Mappings
sections.text: Mapped keyboard W/S keys to control the left player, and arrow keys to control the right player, configuring interactive duels!

recaps.title: Session 12 Recap: Return of Pong and the Ultimate Climax - Part 2! 🏆💥

sections.heading: 💥 Collision Area2D & Scoring
sections.text: Area2D sensors catch ball overlaps to score points, updating scoreboard labels, and multiplying speed by negative one for bounces!

sections.heading: 🎬 Creating Game Trailers
sections.text: A game trailer showcases gameplay highlights in a short video clip to promote our newly published games on itch.io!
